skill.name: commit-work
skill.description: Create focused git commits by reviewing changes, staging only intended work, splitting mixed changes, and writing Conventional Commits messages.
skill.summary: Guide agents through safe staging, focused commit boundaries, and clear Conventional Commits messages.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: The static findings are Markdown command examples for normal git workflows, not executable Ruby or shell code embedded in the skill. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe hidden behavior was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: The workflow includes git commands that can modify staging state or create commits.
remediation.suggestion: State that destructive or history-changing git actions should follow user intent and staged-change review.

static_findings.snippet: - Prefer patch staging for mixed changes: `git add -p`
- To unstage a hunk/file: `git restore --staged -p` or `git restore --staged <path>`
- Prefer an editor for multi-line messages: `git commit -v`
- the commands used to stage/review (at minimum: `git diff --cached`, plus any tests run)

content.value_statement: Messy staging and weak messages slow code review. This skill guides selective staging, commit splitting, Conventional Commits messages, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Reviews git status and diffs before staging work.
Suggests logical commit boundaries for mixed changes.
Uses patch staging guidance for precise commit contents.
Writes Conventional Commits messages with clear what and why context.
Prompts for relevant tests, lint, or build checks before finishing.
limitations: Requires a git repository with accessible working tree state.
Cannot determine project-specific commit rules unless they are provided.
May need user decisions when changes are ambiguous or unrelated.
Does not replace human review of staged changes before committing.

use_cases.title: Prepare a focused bugfix commit
use_cases.description: Review changed files, stage only the bugfix, and write a concise Conventional Commits message.

use_cases.title: Split mixed work for review
use_cases.description: Separate refactors, tests, and feature changes into smaller commits that reviewers can evaluate independently.

use_cases.title: Standardize repository commit history
use_cases.description: Apply consistent message format and verification notes before sharing changes with maintainers.

prompt_templates.title: Commit current work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes, stage the intended work, and create a Conventional Commits message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single clean commit.

prompt_templates.title: Split unrelated changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the working tree and split the changes into logical commits with clear summaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow with multiple change types.

prompt_templates.title: Use project commit rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Create commits using Conventional Commits, a 72-character subject limit, and scopes from this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare review history
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit staged and unstaged changes, propose commit boundaries, run relevant checks, and report final messages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow before opening a pull request.

output_examples.output: One focused fix commit with an authentication scope, a short why-focused body, and the verification command result.

output_examples.input: These changes include formatting, a new endpoint, and tests.
output: A formatting commit for mechanical changes.
A feature commit for the endpoint behavior.
A test commit covering the new endpoint.

output_examples.input: Help me prepare commits before review.
output_examples.output: A staged-change summary, final commit messages, and a short record of checks run before handoff.

best_practices: Inspect unstaged changes before adding files to the index.
Keep each commit focused on one reviewable change.
Run the fastest meaningful verification before finalizing a commit.
anti_patterns: Stage every file without checking the diff.
Mix formatting churn with behavior changes in one commit.
Write messages that only describe implementation details.

faq.question: Does this skill require Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow defaults to Conventional Commits for predictable commit history.

faq.question: Can it split one file across multiple commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends patch staging when separate hunks belong in different commits.

faq.question: Will it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It prompts for the smallest relevant verification and can run checks when the user allows it.

faq.question: Does it protect against committing secrets?
faq.answer: It includes a staged-change review step that checks for secrets, tokens, and accidental debug output.

faq.question: Can it follow custom repository rules?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide subject length, scope, or footer requirements before it writes messages.

faq.question: Is it only for Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is described for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
